newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's May car exports up, local sales stagnant.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's May car exports up, local sales stagnant.

text.p: South Korea's three leading auto makers on Monday reported strong export growth in May as they looked more to overseas markets as a solution to stagnant domestic demand.
But Daewoo Motor Co, a unit of the Daewoo Group, fared well both in domestic and overseas markets, thanks to the recent debut of three new models.
Hyundai Motor Co, South Korea's largest car maker, said its vehicle exports in May rose to 57,130 from 45,437 a year earlier.
"We have reinforced overseas marketing and after-sales services to compensate for falling domestic sales," Hyundai Motor spokesman Min Kyong-hwan said.
Hyundai's overall sales totalled 117,775 vehicles in the month, up slightly from 113,102 a year earlier. Domestic sales fell to 60,645 from 67,665.
Min said domestic sales were dampened by an economic slowdown and rival Daewoo's introduction of new models.
Since last November, Daewoo has introduced Lanos sub-compact, Nubira compact and Leganza mid-sized sedans.
Daewoo Motor Co, a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Group, said vehicle sales in May rose to 86,810 compared with 72,586 a year earlier.
Daewoo's vehicle exports in the month reached 53,565, up from 43,865 a year before.
"Shipments of new model cars contributed to the export rise in May," Daewoo Motor spokesman Lee Chang-won said.
Domestic sales also increased to 33,245 vehicles in May, up from 28,721 a year ago.
Daewoo's emergence as the nation's second largest car seller forced Kia Motors Corp to seek more sales overseas.
Kia said it exported 40,080 vehicles in May, sharply higher than 29,048 a year earlier, while domestic sales dropped to 30,333 from 40,457.
Overall sales rose slightly to 70,413 vehicles in May, against 69,505 a year earlier.
The export rises were backed by the company's efforts to strengthen sales networks in overseas markets, including the United States and Germany, a Kia spokesman said.
"But domestic sales were affected by Daewoo's introduction of new model cars," he said.
South Korea's biggest export markets are the U.S., Europe and Southeast Asia.
Analysts said car makers have been distorting sales figures to hide slackening demand, especially at home.
With high inventories, Korean car companies continued to provide a slew of incentives in May, including non-interest instalment payment schemes.
Analysts said Korean car makers' sales at home were inflated by about 15 percent because they count sales on an ex-factory basis.
"In addition, they force their subcontractors to take cars as payments," said Hur Kang, an analyst at Hyundai Securities.
With many cars sitting idle in parking lots of car makers' outlets, the Korea Automobile Manufacturers' Association decided to release sales figures on the basis of registration by car owners.
